info.desc: Kid A is the fourth studio album by the English rock band Radiohead, released on 2 October 2000 by Parlophone. On the verge of a breakdown after promoting Radiohead's 1997 album OK Computer, songwriter Thom Yorke envisioned a radical change in direction. Radiohead replaced their rock sound with synthesisers, drum machines, the ondes Martenot, string orchestras and brass instruments, incorporating influences from genres such as electronic music, krautrock, jazz, and 20th-century classical music. They recorded Kid A with OK Computer producer Nigel Godrich in Paris, Copenhagen, Gloucestershire and their hometown Oxford, England. The sessions produced over 20 tracks; Radiohead saved .

podcast.body: Considered by Radiohead and Tom Yorke as their best album, "Kid A" marks a significant turning point in the band's career and their most important creative phase. Following the commercial success of "Ok Computer," the band aimed for a more conceptual, complex, and experimental sound, akin to Pink Floyd, intentionally moving away from mass appeal. Its recording process was lengthy, resulting in over 2,000 hours of new material, including songs, small compositions, canned sounds, and demos, which constituted the band's largest creative explosion. "ellos consideran el famoso quida que lo tenemos aquí en su edición el mejor disco de los 10 pulgadas como el álbum que marca un punto de infección en su carrera y el punto más importante."

podcast.body: Radiohead's fourth album, released on October 3, 2000. It emerged after a period of intense pressure and creative block, taking nearly three years to complete following "Okay Computer." The album marked a radical departure in sound, becoming an electronic record with loops, samples, artificial beats, and treated vocals, heavily influenced by techno artists like Aphex Twin and Autechre. During its recording, Ed O'Brien and Jonny Greenwood barely played guitar, and Phil Selway focused more on computer programming. Tom Yorke created the title track's vocals using a self-written computer program, transforming his voice into an instrument. The recording sessions were difficult, moving from Paris to Copenhagen to London and finally to their Oxford private studio. "The fourth album emerged as what can be best described as an electronic record."

podcast.body: Released in 2000, this album features hidden elements within its packaging. Certain editions include a second booklet concealed behind the opaque black tray in the jewel case, containing lyrical snippets that foreshadow future albums. The artwork for the album itself is known to hold interesting secrets. "If you're a fan, you've probably listened to their 2000 CD Kid A a million times, but do you know everything about that record? For example, have you taken apart the jewel case it came in? You should, because certain editions feature a second booklet hidden behind the black opaque tray that holds the disc. ... Radiohead and everything in its right place from Kid A, the artwork of which offers up some interesting secrets."

podcast.body: Released in the fall of 2000, this album is considered a great Radiohead post-rock album, described as atmospheric, cinematic, and a sonic journey. It was the follow-up to *OK Computer*, and its first single surprised everyone. "If I were to point to a great Radiohead post-rock album, I would go with Kid A from the fall of 2000."

podcast.body: The band's famous bear logo first gained public attention through television advertisements for the launch of this album, referred to as "Qidei" in the transcript. These ads featured a static image of the bear's face. Additionally, the bear comic, consisting of about 15 vignettes, was circulated informally across the web during the period of this album's release. "el anuncio de televisión del lanzamiento del Qidei era una imagen estática con esta cara de este osso."

podcast.body: The iconic bear symbol became associated with Radiohead since their album "Qtay" (Kid A), stemming from the brilliant concept art created by Estal Lidon Boot for that record. This symbol predominantly appeared on bootlegs and merchandise rather than the studio album's cover. "este iconico osos ha asociado a Radiohead desde su álbum Qtay a raíz del genial concept art de ese disco, realizado por el Estal Lidon Boot."

podcast.body: The release of "Kid A" just months before Mios's "Origin of Symetry" in 2001 ignited a "fever" in the UK for experimental electronic progressive rock. This contributed to the challenging market conditions for Mios's more guitar-driven sound. "Justo unos meses antes del lanzamiento Origin of Symetry salía el quide y de Radiohead con lo cual se desatabó en una especie de furor dentro del reino unido por ese rock experimental el electrónico progresivo a raro uno se desatabó en auténtica fiebre después del quide y dentro del reino unido."

podcast.body: This album showcased a pervasive IDM influence from beginning to end, marking the genre's expansion to a more mainstream audience. To prepare for its creation, lead singer Thom Yorke acquired the entire catalog of Warp Records for inspiration. "Finalmente el idm acabó llegando a un policón más masivo, con Qtid de Radiohead, donde se percibe su influencia de principio a fin."

srcs.episode: Qué fue el IDM y por qué cambió la música electrónica

podcast.body: This album was initially met with severe criticism, with many considering it the "end of Radiohead's career." Despite these initial reactions, "Kid A" ultimately became a new, even more exciting trajectory for the band, demonstrating that radical changes can lead to creative resurgence. "Cuando los irroydios sacaron el Qidei, muchos seréis muy jóvenes, pero yo recuerdo las críticas del Qidei lo consideraban el final de la carrera de Radiohead, y al final ha sido una nueva trayectoria casi casi más apasionante que anterior."

podcast.body: This album, along with `Amnesiac` and `Hail to the Thief`, marked Thom Yorke's "greatest creative explosion." The recording process involved marathon sessions over several months, accumulating thousands of hours of material, some of which later contributed to Thom Yorke's solo work. "la mayor explosión creativa que tuvo Tom Jorken toda su vida fue la que grabó en la gran triilogía del quidad de la amnesia y de la emite y ron."
This album, released in 2000, features the song "Idioteque." "There's Radiohead's Idiotique from Kidei in 2000."
